1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height, and codes/secrets are set in letter-spaced monospace.

2.why: Guidance text is sentence-case with no italics and short blocks; the only dense text is the non-instructional provisioning URI line in step 4.

3.why: The mock provisioning URI on the Confirm authenticator screen overflows the card horizontally, so content is not fully readable and well laid out at mobile width.

4.why: Most instructions are one plain sentence (e.g., 'Generate a secret, then add it manually'), though the step-4 note uses jargon like 'adjacent period for limited clock skew'.

5.why: Placeholders show example formats for most inputs ('marcus@example.test', 'ABCDE-23456'), but the OTP fields only say 'Six digits' rather than showing a sample value.

6.why: No screen forces the user to read a long passage; the longest text is an optional four-line informational note.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as selectable text and the UI says 'Copy them now', but no one-tap copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code appears anywhere; the only alternative is a raw, overflowing otpauth URI string that still must be handled manually.

9.why: Standard email/password fields should work with password managers, but nothing observable (e.g., one-time-code autofill on OTP fields) demonstrates autofill support.

10.why: Each enrolment screen shows a 'Step X of 5' pill and one dominant blue button, though on the settings page the red Log out button visually competes with the primary actions.

11.why: Every flow step requests a single action (Continue, Verify, Confirm, Save), while the settings page merely lists optional self-initiated actions.

12.why: Plain status lines follow actions ('Recovery code accepted and consumed.', 'You have been logged out.') and each screen states what to do next.

13.why: Failed steps can be retried ('Please try again') and recovery codes can be regenerated with no shown penalty, though there is no reveal/hide toggle or SMS resend control.

14.why: The only observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but generic and never states what the actual problem was.

15.why: Step 4 imposes a five-minute setup expiry and 30-second code rotation, so code entry is time-limited rather than untimed and generous.
